To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the IP3R is spliced in a tissue-specific manner and the spliced form is selectively expressed in neurons.

the rat IP3R1 gene exhibits alternative splicing of a 40 amino acids insert between two sites of phosphorylation, that this splicing is selectively expressed in neuronal tissues, and that the presence or absence of the insert changes the site of phosphorylation by PKA.

the inositol 1,4, 5-trisphosphate receptor (IP3R) is alternatively spliced at a site located between two sites for phosphorylation of the rat receptor by protein kinase A (PKA) and that the splice is selectively expressed in neurons.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the characterization of the inositol(1,4, 5)-tris-phosphate receptor (IP3R), a calcium channel that mediates the mobilization of calcium from internal stores in response to stimulation of the phosphoinositide signaling system.
the regulation of intracellular calcium release through the inositol 1,4, 5-trisphosphate receptors.
the molecular biology of the IP3 receptor, a Ca2+ channel that is a key component of the Ca2+ signaling pathway that mediates a number of cellular responses.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there are 3 splice variants of IP3R in the rat, and that they are differentially expressed in the brain and peripheral tissues.

there is a single receptor isoform expressed in the rat, and that it is the same isoform that is expressed in the mouse, and that the isoforms differ only in the presence or absence of a 40 amino-acid insert.
the IP3R splice isoform containing the 40 amino acid sequence is expressed in neurons, but not in non-neuronal tissues.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the rat IP3R is alternatively spliced to generate two major forms, one containing a 40 amino-acid insert and the other not.

the rat IP3R1 gene is alternatively spliced in neurons to generate a receptor with an insert that changes the preferred site for PKA phosphorylation, and that the degree of this splicing differs between rat and mouse.
there are at least four major forms of the IP3R: a long form containing the insert, a short form lacking it, and two forms that lack the insert but are differentially phosphorylated by PKA.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the IP3R splice variants are expressed in a tissue- and cell type-specific manner.

there are significant species differences in the regulation of the alternative splicing in the IP3R gene, suggesting that this gene may be under selective pressure to adapt its splicing pattern to the needs of the organism.
the IP3R is an example of a gene whose expression is highly regulated by alternative splicing.
